item.description: Research shows dental sealants to shield the back teeth could prevent up to 80 percent of cavities in school-aged children. They are quick, easy, and painless to apply - yet according to a new CDC Vital Signs, about 60 percent of school children ages 6-11 years don't get dental sealants.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Media Advisory
item.description: According to the new Vital Signs report, dental sealants prevent 80% of cavities in school-age children, particularly for the back teeth, where 9 in 10 cavities occur. About 60% of children ages 6-11 don't get dental sealants.

item.title: CDC working with Florida to respond to new active Zika transmission area in Miami-Dade County - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) continues to work with Florida health officials to investigate new cases of locally transmitted Zika virus infection in Miami-Dade County.

item.title: New CDC study shows changes in breast cancer death rates by age group - Press Release
item.description: Breast cancer death rates among women decreased during 2010-2014, but racial differences persisted, according to a study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in this week's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

item.title: Contaminated Devices Putting Open-Heart Surgery Patients at Risk - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is warning healthcare providers and patients about the potential risk of infection from certain devices used during open heart (open-chest) surgery.

item.title: CDC funds 34 innovative projects to combat antibiotic resistance - Press Release
item.description: CDC has awarded more than $14 million to fund new approaches to combat antibiotic resistance, including research on how microorganisms naturally present in the human body (referred to as a person's microbiome) can be used to predict and prevent infections caused by drug-resistant organisms.

item.title: CDC updates interim guidance for pre-pregnancy counseling and prevention of sexual transmission of Zika - Media Statement
item.description: CDC today announced updates to its interim guidance for pre-pregnancy counseling and prevention of sexual transmission of Zika based on ongoing assessment of available data, primarily extending the timeframe for men with possible Zika exposure but no Zika symptoms to wait before attempting pregnancy with their partner and extending the time for use of condoms by these men to protect against sexual transmission of Zika virus infection.

item.title: CDC issues Zika special travel considerations for 11 Southeast Asian countries
item.description: Today, CDC posted Zika virus-related special travel considerations for 11 Southeastern Asian countries. CDC now recommends that pregnant women should consider postponing nonessential travel to these countries because of the uncertain risk of Zika virus infection. CDC is issuing these special travel considerations so that travelers, especially pregnant women, can make informed decisions about their travel and their health.

item.title: Influenza Outlook 2016-2017: What You Should Know about Flu Prevention This Season - Media Advisory
item.description: Tom Frieden, M.D., M.P.H., director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), joined by other medical and public health experts, will address the nation in preparation for the upcoming flu season at a news conference presented by the National Foundation for Infectious Diseases (NFID).

item.title: Dialysis organizations team up with CDC to protect patients - Press Release
item.description: CDC is teaming up with a broad coalition of kidney and dialysis organizations to reduce the number of bloodstream infections in dialysis patients. Each year, about 37,000 people get potentially deadly bloodstream infections related to their dialysis treatment.

item.title: CDC awards $13 million to establish the first Vector Control Unit in Puerto Rico - Media Statement
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) today announced that it has awarded $13 million to the Puerto Rico Science, Technology, and Research Trust (ST&R Trust) to establish the first Vector Control Unit (VCU) in Puerto Rico ...

item.title: CDC adds St. Kitts and Nevis to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing spread of Zika virus?. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for St. Kitts and Nevis.

item.title: Transcript for CDC Telebriefing: Zika Telebriefing Update - Transcript
item.description: CDC hosted a telebriefing on Zika

item.title: Florida health officials report on response to Zika in Wynwood; evidence shows aerial spraying likely helped interrupt local transmission - Media Statement
item.description: Florida health officials' response this summer to the first identified cases of local transmission and the first identified outbreak of Zika virus infection in the continental United States, including aggressive mosquito control efforts, helped to interrupt local transmission and reduce the effect on the community, including pregnant women.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: Zika Virus Update - 09-23-2016 - Media Advisory
item.description: Florida health officials' response this summer to the first identified cases of local transmission and the first identified outbreak of Zika virus infection in the continental United States, including aggressive mosquito control efforts, helped to stop local transmission and reduce the effect on the community, including pregnant women.

item.title: Falls are leading cause of injury and death in older Americans - Press Release
item.description: Every second of every day in the United States an older adult falls, making falls the number one cause of injuries and deaths from injury among older Americans.

item.title: Celebrating 70 years: 12th annual Smithsonian magazine Museum Day Live! - Media Advisory
item.description: Celebrating 70 years: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention will take part in the 12th annual Smithsonian magazine Museum Day Live! event. The David J. Sencer CDC Museum will join other Smithsonian Institution affiliates across the country for this annual one-day event.

item.title: CDC continues to build US laboratory capacity to rapidly detect Zika virus infection - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has purchased approximately $2.5 million in laboratory supplies and equipment in August to enhance U.S. laboratory (lab) capacity to test for Zika virus.

item.title: CDC updates guidance for Wynwood (FL) neighborhood with active Zika transmission - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has updated guidance for people who travel to or live in the approximately 1-square-mile area in Wynwood, Florida, just north of downtown Miami.

item.title: CDC works with Florida as Miami Beach active Zika transmission area expands
item.description: The Florida Department of Health (DOH) has confirmed through its ongoing investigation that there is active mosquito-borne spread of Zika virus in a larger section of Miami Beach.

item.title: Adults Need More Activity - Digital Press Kit
item.description: Regular physical activity is vital for healthy aging. It can help delay, prevent, or manage many costly chronic diseases. Physical activity can also reduce the risk of premature death.

item.title: More than 1 in 4 US adults over 50 do not engage in regular physical activity - Press Release
item.description: Despite the many benefits of moderate physical activity, 31 million Americans (28 percent) age 50 years and older are inactive - that is, they are not physically active beyond the basic movements needed for daily life activities.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Poor blood-pressure control puts more than 5 million people at risk: How can health care systems help people take their medicine as directed? - Media Advisory
item.description: According to the latest CDC Vital Signs report, about 70% of US adults age 65 or older have high blood pressure - but only about half have it under control (less than 140/90), putting them at risk of heart disease, stroke, and early death.

item.title: CDC awards $2.4 million to five jurisdictions to fight Zika - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has awarded $2.4 million to Chicago, Houston, New York City, Philadelphia, and Los Angeles County to establish, enhance, and maintain information-gathering systems to rapidly detect microcephaly-a serious birth defect of the brain-and other adverse outcomes linked to Zika virus infection.

item.title: CDC and the Instituto Nacional de Salud of Colombia collaborate to understand long-term effects of Zika virus infection during pregnancy - Press Release
item.description: CDC Director Tom Frieden, MD, MPH, and Martha Lucía Ospina Martínez, MD, MPH, MBA, Director General of Colombia's Instituto Nacional de Salud (INS), have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to collaborate on Zika virus response activities in Colombia, particularly the effect of Zika virus during pregnancy.

item.title: New Obesity Maps Show US Adults Still Struggle with Obesity - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC today released 2015 state- and territory-specific data on adult obesity prevalence using self-reported information from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS).

item.title: Two thirds of US adults believe pharmacies should not sell tobacco - Press Release
item.description: Two-thirds of American adults believe pharmacies should not be allowed to sell tobacco, while 14 percent strongly oppose such a policy, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) ...

item.title: Traces of Ebola Virus Linger Longer than Expected in Semen - Press Release
item.description: Initial data from a Liberian public health program show about 9 percent (38) of 429 male Ebola survivors had fragments of Ebola virus in their semen.

item.title: CDC adds Singapore to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for Singapore. CDC has issued travel notices (level 2, "practice enhanced precautions") for people traveling to destinations with Zika. For a full list of affected countries/regions, visit http://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/page/zika-travel-information.

item.title: CDC adds The British Virgin Islands to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for The British Virgin Islands. Local transmission of Zika has been reported on the island of Tortola, which includes Cane Garden Bay and Havers.

item.title: CDC releases genetic data on antibiotic resistant Salmonella infections - Media Statement
item.description: For the first time, the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) annual report includes whole genome sequencing (WGS) data of bacteria from people with antibiotic-resistant Salmonella infections.

item.title: CDC continues to support Florida in response to Zika outbreak - Press Release
item.description: CDC has and will continue to provide support to Florida to address the Zika outbreak. CDC experts in epidemiology, surveillance, and vector control have been on the ground for weeks supporting the state of Florida's response.

item.title: CDC Foundation's New Business Pulse Focuses on On-the-Job Vehicle Crashes - Media Advisory
item.description: Business Pulse: Motor Vehicle Safety at Work, launched today by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Foundation, focuses on how businesses can protect employees who drive for work in the United States and travel for business abroad.

item.title: CDC awards $6.8 million to partners to support Zika response - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has awarded $6.8 million to national public health partners to assist state, tribal, local, and territorial jurisdictions with their Zika responses in a wide range of activities, including surveillance and epidemiology, vector control, communication and outreach to pregnant women and vulnerable populations, and planning with key stakeholders.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - How can we save patients from sepsis? - Transcript
item.description: CDC hosted a telebriefing on sepsis.

item.title: CDC adds The Bahamas to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for The Bahamas. Local transmission of Zika has been reported on the island of New Providence, which includes the capital city of Nassau.

item.title: Saving patients from sepsis is a race against time - Press Release
item.description: Sepsis is caused by the body's overwhelming and life-threatening response to an infection and requires rapid intervention. It begins outside of the hospital for nearly 80 percent of patients.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - How can we save patients from sepsis? - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC will release a Vital Signs report focusing on sepsis, emphasizing the importance of prevention and early recognition. Sepsis is a complication caused by the body's overwhelming and life-threatening response to infection, which can lead to tissue damage, organ failure, and death.

item.title: Breastfeeding Rates Continue To Rise - Press Release
item.description: In the United States, more than 8 in 10 mothers (81.1 percent) begin breastfeeding their babies at birth - but many stop earlier than is recommended, according to the 2016 Breastfeeding Report Card released today by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: Zika Virus Update - August 19 - Transcript
item.description: CDC hosted a telebriefing to provide an update on the Zika virus

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: Zika Virus Update - 8-19-2016 - Media Advisory
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has been working with Florida health officials on investigating cases of locally transmitted Zika virus. The most recent information suggests that there may be a new active Zika transmission in South Florida.

item.title: Additional area of active Zika transmission identified in Miami Beach - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has been working with Florida health officials on investigating cases of locally transmitted Zika virus. An additional area of active Zika transmission has been identified in a section of Miami Beach, in addition to the area of active Zika transmission near Wynwood.

item.title: CDC Updates Guidance for Care of Infants Born to Mothers with Possible Zika Virus Infection During Pregnancy - Media Statement
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) today issued updated interim clinical guidance for health care providers caring for infants born to mothers with possible Zika virus infection during pregnancy.

item.title: Improper care of contact lenses can cause serious eye infections - Press Release
item.description: Nearly 1 in 5 contact lens-related eye infections reported to a federal database involved a patient who experienced eye damage, according to a report published in CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.title: Statement from CDC Director Tom Frieden on the passing of Shane Todd, former Tips From Former Smokers campaign participant - Media Statement
item.description: We are deeply saddened by the passing of our friend Shane Todd from complications of cancer at the age of 49. Shane was just 34 years old when he was diagnosed with throat cancer caused by the cigarette smoking he began at 18.

item.title: Two Cases of Polio Detected in Nigeria - Media Statement
item.description: Two children have been diagnosed with polio in Nigeria, after two years without any polio recognized in that country. Polio is a terrible disease that no child should suffer.

item.title: CDC adds Cayman Islands to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for Cayman Islands. CDC has issued travel notices (level 2, "practice enhanced precautions") for people traveling to destinations with Zika. For a full list of affected countries/regions, visit http://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/page/zika-travel-information.

item.title: National ALS Registry Releases Updated Prevalence Estimates - Press Release
item.description: The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry's (ATSDR) National ALS Registry today released its second report on the prevalence of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, commonly known as Lou Gehrig's disease) in the United States for the years 2012 and 2013.

item.title: Some racial, ethnic groups continue smoking cigarettes at higher rates - Press Release
item.description: Despite a significant decline in overall adult cigarette smoking since 1964, disparities in cigarette smoking remain among racial and ethnic population groups, according to a new study from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) published in today's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.title: CDC adds Antigua and Barbuda and Turks and Caicos Islands (U.K.) to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for Antigua and Barbuda as well as Turks and Caicos Islands (U.K.).

item.title: CDC Announces new director of Division of Select Agents and Toxins - Media Statement
item.description: CDC announces today the selection of Samuel S. Edwin, Ph.D., to become the new director of the agency's Division of Select Agents and Toxins (DSAT).

item.description: Funding provided for states and territories to respond to the emerging threat, quickly identify cases of microcephaly and other adverse birth outcomes linked to Zika, ...

item.description: New assessments of mosquito populations and test results this past weekend by Florida public health officials, as part of a community survey in the Miami neighborhood where several Zika infections were recently confirmed, have found persistent mosquito populations and additional Zika infections in the same area.

item.description: Transcript for CDC telebriefing that to provided an update on the Zika virus.

item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has been informed by the State of Florida that Zika virus infections in four people were likely caused by bites of local Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.

item.title: Zika infections increasing rapidly in Puerto Rico - Press Release
item.description: As of July 7, Zika has been diagnosed in 5,582* people, including 672 pregnant women, in Puerto Rico according to a new report published today in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.description: CDC will host a telebriefing to provide an update on the Zika virus

item.description: CDC is providing $67 million to help health departments nationwide tackle antibiotic resistance and other patient safety threats, including healthcare-associated infections.

item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for Saba.

item.description: CDC today issued updated guidance and information to prevent Zika virus transmission and health effects.

item.title: CDC awards $60 million to help states and territories battle Zika - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) will begin making awards totaling nearly $60 million to states, cities, and territories to support efforts to protect Americans from Zika virus disease and adverse health outcomes that can result from Zika infection, including the serious birth defect microcephaly.

item.title: Webcast: Clinical Evaluation & Management of Infants with Congenital Zika Infection - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC will host a meeting in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics.

item.title: CDC assisting Utah investigation of Zika virus infection apparently not linked to travel - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is assisting in the investigation of a case of Zika in a Utah resident who is a family contact of the elderly Utah resident who died in late June.

item.title: CDC Media Availability: Support for Utah investigation of Zika - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC will host a media availability to answer questions from reporters about the case of Zika reported by Utah health officials.

item.title: CDC Joins Global Leaders in New Partnership to End Violence Against Children - Media Advisory
item.description: The new partnership supports individuals and groups working to prevent and respond to violence; protect childhood; and make societies safe for children.

item.title: First female-to-male sexual transmission of Zika virus infection reported in New York City - Media Statement
item.description: The New York City report of female-to-male sexual transmission of Zika virus infection is the first documented case of sexual transmission of Zika from a woman to her sex partner...

item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for St. Eustatius.

item.description: According to the Brazilian Tourism Board, approximately 350,000 - 500,000 international visitors and athletes from 207 countries are expected to travel to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil for the 2016 Olympic and Paralympic Games (Games).

item.title: Tobacco use, involuntary secondhand smoke exposure high in multiunit housing residents - Press Release
item.description: Americans living in multiunit housing, such as apartments and condominiums, are more likely to use tobacco products and less likely to have smoke-free home rules than people living in single-family housing, according to a new study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: Motor Vehicle Crash Deaths - Transcript
item.description: Transcript and audio file of CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Where does the U.S. stand in crash death rates compared with other high-income countries?

item.title: CDC Releases Detailed History of the 2014-2016 Ebola Response in MMWR - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) today will release a detailed account of the agency's work on the largest, longest outbreak response in the agency's history: the Ebola epidemic of 2014-2016. The series of articles, in a special supplement to CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR), comes on the second anniversary of the official activation of the agency's emergency response to Ebola.

item.title: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Environmental Protection Agency Urge Commonwealth of Puerto Rico to Consider Aerial Spraying as Part of Integrated Mosquito Control to Reduce Zika-Associated Birth Defects - Media Statement
item.description: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) recommend the people and the government of Puerto Rico consider implementing aerial spraying as part of an integrated mosquito control program.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Where does the U.S. stand in crash death rates compared with other high-income countries? - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC Telebriefing on the new Vital Signs focused on where the US stands in crash deaths, in relation to other high-income countries.

item.title: Motor vehicle crash fatalities in the U.S. could drop by half with proven strategies - Press Release
item.description: About 90 people die each day from motor vehicle crashes in the United States, resulting in the highest death rate among 19 high-income comparison countries.

item.title: CDC Awards $30 Million to 23 state injury and violence prevention programs - Media Advisory
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) announced today it will award $30 million to 23 state health departments over the next five years as part of the Core State Violence and Injury Prevention Program (Core SVIPP).

item.title: CDC Awards Funds for States and Territories to Prepare for Zika - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has awarded $25 million in funding to states, cities, and territories to support efforts to protect Americans from Zika virus infection and associated adverse health outcomes, including microcephaly and the other serious birth defects.

item.title: Federal Select Agent Program first annual report released - Media Advisory
item.description: The Federal Select Agent Program (FSAP) released today its first annual report of data on the regulation and oversight of laboratories that work with biological agents and toxins that have the potential to pose a severe threat to public, animal or plant health, or to animal or plant products (select agents and toxins).

item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus transmission. Today, CDC posted a Zika virus travel notice for Anguilla.

item.description: Finding points way to new approaches to Ebola treatment

item.title: CDC Awards $26 Million to Academic Medical Centers, Drives Innovation to Protect Patients - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has awarded $26 million to support applied research at five academic medical centers as part of a patient safety effort known as Prevention Epicenters Program.

item.title: Global Health Security - Liberia
item.description: Building Response Capabilities in Liberia after Ebola

item.title: CDC investigation: Blood lead levels higher after switch to Flint River water - Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) today released the results of its investigation into the potential health impact that lead contamination in the Flint, Michigan water supply had on the blood lead levels of local children.

item.title: Southeastern states not protected by comprehensive smoke-free laws - Press Release
item.description: Ten years after the Surgeon General's report on the dangers of exposure to secondhand tobacco smoke, no states in the Southeast have a statewide comprehensive smoke-free law, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) published in today's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.title: ACIP votes down use of LAIV for 2016-2017 flu season - Media Statement
item.description: CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) today voted that live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV), also known as the "nasal spray" flu vaccine, should not be used during the 2016-2017 flu season.

item.title: CDC Foundation's New Business Pulse Focuses on Rising Health Care Costs - Media Advisory
item.description: Business Pulse: Lowering Costs, Improving Productivity, launched today by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Foundation, focuses on how businesses can tackle the burden of rising health care costs.

item.title: U.S. healthcare facilities have capacity to meet colorectal cancer screening goals - Press Release
item.description: US government agencies and their colorectal cancer prevention partners have set a goal that at least 80% of adults ages 50-75 will be screened for colorectal cancer.

item.title: CDC launches first national reporting system for harmful algal blooms and associated illnesses - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC launched the first national reporting system for harmful algal blooms, as well as a new website with important information for health officials and the public.

item.description: Transcripts for CDC Telebriefing Zika Screening Blood Donations for Zika Virus to Protect Blood Update

item.description: New supplement from the American Journal of Preventive Medicine describes the state of sickle cell disease related care in the United States.

item.description: CDC published interim guidance for Zika virus antibody testing and interpretation of results. Because of the differences in recommended clinical management of Zika and dengue virus infections, and the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in women infected with Zika virus during pregnancy, a conservative approach to the interpretation of antibody test results is necessary to reduce the possibility of a missed diagnosis of either infections.

item.title: Hepatitis C Kills More Americans than Any Other Infectious Disease - Press Release

These recommendations provide information to travelers to help them take steps to stay safe and healthy during their trips. CDC's travel guidance for the Olympics covers a variety of health and safety topics, including information about the Zika virus outbreak currently occurring in Brazil. Because of the Zika outbreak, CDC recommends that pregnant women consider not traveling to the Olympics.

These data were presented at a meeting of the agency's Advisory Committee for Immunization Practices (ACIP) in Atlanta. This finding is comparable to past estimates for seasons when most circulating flu viruses and vaccine viruses have been similar.

item.title: New Lyme-disease-causing bacteria species discovered- Press Release
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, in collaboration with Mayo Clinic and health officials from Minnesota, Wisconsin, and North Dakota, report the discovery of a new species of bacteria (Borrelia mayonii) that causes Lyme disease in people. Until now, Borrelia burgdorferi was the only species believed to cause Lyme disease in North America.

item.title: Teen Dating Violence Awareness & Prevention Month - Digital Press Kit

item.title: Zika Virus - Digital Press Kit

The illness is usually mild with symptoms lasting from several days to a week. Severe disease requiring hospitalization is uncommon.

item.description: CDC has issued new interim guidance on preventing sexual transmission of Zika virus after confirming through laboratory testing, in collaboration with Dallas County Health and Human Services, the first case of Zika virus infection in a non-traveler in the continental United States during this outbreak.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New and Updated Interim Guidance for Zika virus - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC is issuing interim guidelines for preventing sexual transmission of Zika virus and updated interim guidance for health care providers caring for pregnant women and women of reproductive age with possible Zika virus exposure

item.title: Transcript for CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Why are millions of US women at risk of alcohol-exposed pregnancies? - Transcript
item.description: Transcript for CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Why are millions of US women at risk of alcohol-exposed pregnancies?

item.title: CDC adds 2 destinations to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC added the following destinations to the Zika virus travel alerts: Jamaica and Tonga

item.title: More than 3 million US women at risk for alcohol-exposed pregnancy- Press Release
item.description: An estimated 3.3 million women between the ages of 15 and 44 years are at risk of exposing their developing baby to alcohol because they are drinking, sexually active, and not using birth control to prevent pregnancy, according to the latest CDC Vital Signs report released today.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Why are millions of US women at risk of alcohol-exposed pregnancies? - Media Advisory
item.description: More than 3 million women between the ages of 15 and 44 years are at risk of exposing their developing baby to alcohol because they are drinking and not using birth control to prevent pregnancy, according to the latest CDC Vital Signs report.

item.title: CDC adds 4 destinations to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC added the following destinations to the Zika virus travel alerts: American Samoa, Costa Rica, Curacao, and Nicaragua.

item.title: Transcript: Zika Virus Travel Alert
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases will discuss the latest on Zika virus.

item.title: CDC-NIAID Telebriefing: Zika 101 - Media Advisory
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases will discuss the latest on Zika virus..

item.title: CDC adds 2 destinations to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC added the following destinations to the Zika virus travel alerts: United States Virgin Islands and Dominican Republic.

item.title: CDC Museum to Host Places & Spaces: Mapping Science Exhibition - Media Statement
item.description: From January 25 to June 17, 2016, the David J. Sencer CDC Museum will feature the Places & Spaces: Mapping Science exhibition showing how data visualization helps us confront some of the world's most significant challenges.

item.title: CDC adds countries to interim travel guidance related to Zika virus - Media Statement
item.description: CDC is working with other public health officials to monitor for ongoing Zika virus? transmission. Today, CDC added the following destinations to the Zika virus travel alerts: Barbados, Bolivia, Ecuador, Guadeloupe, Saint Martin, Guyana, Cape Verde, and Samoa.

item.title: Continued increase in birth defect of abdominal wall - Press Release
item.description: Cases of a serious birth defect of the abdominal wall called gastroschisis continues to increase over time, according to a report in CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

item.title: First-of-its-Kind PSA Campaign Targets the 86 Million American Adults with Prediabetes - Press Release
item.description: American Diabetes Association, American Medical Association, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Ad Council Join Forces to Reduce the Incidence of Type 2 Diabetes, One of the Nation's Biggest Public Health Crises Today

item.title: Powerful new ads mark the 5th year of the successful "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign - Press Release
item.description: A brand-new series of emotionally powerful ads kick off the fifth year of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign.

item.title: Transcript for CDC Telebriefing: Zika Virus Travel Alert - Transcript
item.description: CDC issues interim travel guidance related to Zika virus for 14 Countries and Territories in Central and South America and the Caribbean

item.title: CDC issues interim travel guidance related to Zika virus for 14 Countries and Territories in Central and South America and the Caribbean - Media Statement

Media Statement
For Immediate Release: Friday, January 15, 2016 Contact: Media Relations, (404) 639-3286
CDC has issued a travel alert (Level 2-Practice Enhanced Precautions) for people traveling to regions and certain countries where Zika virus transmission is ongoing: Brazil, Colombia, El Salvador, French Guiana, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Martinique, Mexico, Panama, Paraguay, Suriname, Venezuela, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: Interim travel guidance for Zika virus - Media Advisory
item.description: CDC is issuing interim travel guidance for areas with ongoing Zika virus transmission.

item.title: New Research: Excess Sodium Intake Remains Common in the United States - Press Release
item.description: Nearly all Americans - regardless of age, race, gender or whether they have high blood pressure (hypertension) - consume more sodium than is recommended for a healthy diet. That is the conclusion of a new report published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in today's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Why is youth e-cigarette advertising harmful for youth? - Transcript
item.description: Transcript of the Vital Signs report telebriefing on e-cigarette advertising to middle and high school students.

item.title: New CDC Vital Signs: E-cigarette Ads and Youth - Digital Press Kit
item.description: About 7 in 10 middle and high school students - more than 18 million young people - see e-cigarette advertising in stores, online, in newspapers and magazines, or on television and in movies, according to a new CDC Vital Signs report.

item.title: E-cigarette ads reach nearly 7 in 10 middle and high-school students - Press Release
item.description: About 7 in 10 middle and high school students - more than 18 million young people - see e-cigarette advertising in stores, online, in newspapers and magazines, or on television and in movies, according to a new CDC Vital Signs report.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report - Why is youth e-cigarette advertising harmful for youth? - Media Advisory
item.description: In 2014, e-cigarettes became the most commonly used tobacco product among youth, surpassing conventional cigarettes. During 2011 to 2014, current e-cigarette use among high school students soared from 1.5 percent to 13.4 percent, and among middle school students from 0.6 percent to 3.9 percent. What can states and communities do to reduce this trend?

item.title: First case of Zika virus reported in Puerto Rico - Media Statement
item.description: The Puerto Rico Department of Health reported today the first locally acquired case of Zika virus infection in Puerto Rico. Zika was confirmed in a resident of Puerto Rico with no known travel history.

item.title: Enhanced Entry Airport Screening for Ebola Modified for Travelers from Guinea to the United States
item.description: On Dec. 29, 2015, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) will modify enhanced Ebola port-of-entry screening for travelers from Guinea.

item.title: CDC Year in Review: What's Next? - Press Release
item.description: In a digital press kit released today, CDC reviews the most pressing public health challenges of 2015 and previews plans for 2016.

item.title: CDC To Play Key Role in National Multidrug-Resistant TB Plan - Media Statement
item.description: Today, the White House released the "National Action Plan to Combat Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR TB)". This plan is a crucial step to address MDR TB, a growing public health threat that reflects missed opportunities to find, cure, and prevent TB.

item.title: Enhanced Entry Airport Screening for Ebola to End for Travelers from Sierra Leone to the United States - Media Statement
item.description: On Dec. 22, 2015, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) will remove Sierra Leone from the list of nations affected by Ebola that are subject to enhanced visa and port-of-entry screening.

item.title: Drug overdose deaths hit record numbers in 2014 - Press Release
item.description: From 2000 to 2014 nearly half a million Americans died from drug overdoses. Opioid overdose deaths, including both opioid pain relievers and heroin, hit record levels in 2014, with an alarming 14 percent increase in just one year, according to new data published today in CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

item.title: Half of those who need them not taking cholesterol-lowering medications - Press Release
item.description: More than a third of American adults are eligible to take cholesterol-lowering medications under the current guidelines or were already taking them - but nearly half of them are not, according to a report by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention researchers published in the current issue of Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.title: Transcript for CDC Telebriefing: Daily Pill Prevents HIV - Transcript
item.description: New CDC estimates underscore the need to increase awareness of a daily pill that can prevent HIV infection

item.title: Daily Pill Prevents HIV - Reaching People Who Could Benefit From PrEP
item.description: CDC's latest Vital Signs report finds a continuing need to raise awareness of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) - a daily pill that can prevent HIV infection - among those who are at substantial risk for HIV infection.

item.title: New CDC estimates underscore the need to increase awareness of a daily pill that can prevent HIV infection - Press Release
item.description: A new Vital Signs report published today estimates that 25 percent of sexually active gay and bisexual adult men, nearly 20 percent of adults who inject drugs, and less than 1 percent of heterosexually active adults are at substantial risk for HIV infection and should be counseled about PrEP, a daily pill for HIV prevention.

item.title: CDC Telebriefing: New Vital Signs Report When is a daily pill the right option to prevent HIV? - Media Advisory
item.description: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is one essential component in the nation's high-impact prevention strategy for HIV. Many people at very high risk for HIV infection are not getting PrEP and not enough primary health care providers know about it.

item.title: CDC Foundation's New Business Pulse Focuses on Workplace Safety - Media Advisory
item.description: Business Pulse: Workplace Safety and Health, launched today by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Foundation, focuses on innovative employer strategies using science-based solutions from CDC's National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) to address emerging worker safety and health issues and well-recognized workplace hazards and exposures.

item.title: CDC responds to broad challenges facing US cancer survivors - Press Release
item.description: The number of cancer survivors - people who live after a cancer diagnosis - is expected to grow substantially over the next few decades as the U.S. population ages and as early detection methods and treatments continue to improve.

item.title: Get Smart About Antibiotics Week 2015 - Digital Press Kit
item.description: GET SMART ABOUT ANTIBIOTICS WEEK, an annual one-week observance starting on Monday, November 16, raises awareness of the threat of antibiotic resistance and the importance of improving antibiotic use.

item.title: More than 120 Partners Join CDC to Fight Antibiotic Resistance - Press Release
item.description: The President has proclaimed Nov. 16-22 "Get Smart About Antibiotics Week." Get Smart Week builds on the momentum generated at the White House Forum on Antibiotic Stewardship, where more than 150 organizations pledged to improve antibiotic use and slow the spread of antibiotic resistance.

item.title: Smoking rates for uninsured and adults on Medicaid more than twice those for adults with private health insurance - Press Release
item.description: American adults who are uninsured or on Medicaid smoke at rates more than double those for adults with private health insurance or Medicare, according to a study published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in today's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR).

item.title: Modifications to Enhanced Entry Airport Screening for Travelers from Sierra Leone to the United States - Media Statement
item.description: On November 10, 2015, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) will modify enhanced Ebola port-of-entry screening for travelers from Sierra Leone.

item.title: World Health Organization Declares Sierra Leone Free of Ebola Virus Transmission - Media Statement
